newsitem.title: POLAND: Bank Gdanski sells stake in motorway firm.
newsitem.headline: Bank Gdanski sells stake in motorway firm.

text.p: Poland's Bank Gdanski has sold its stake in a company bidding in a motorway construction tender to farming bank Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ), BGZ said in a statement on Monday.

BGZ spokeswoman Agnieszka Jaworska later told Reuters that after the sale the company, Gdansk Transport Company SA, would be controlled by BGZ, Polish construction firm GPRD SA and U.S.-based Bechtel Inc.
"Together with GPRD and Bechtel Inc, we are the main shareholder in the company, with the same number of shares," Jaworska told Reuters. She gave no further details.

Gdansk Transport Company SA is currently the sole bidder in the tender to build the 152-km A-1 motorway between the northern cities of Gdansk and Torun. The tender is due to be concluded later this year.
The project is part of Poland's $8 billion programme to build 2,500 km of toll motorways within 15 years.
